additions.what: Added 'what if we could view this training process as evolving the output distribution itself' and 'Consider how the distribution of generated samples changes as training progresses' to problem_context
additions.why: The student is still thinking about distilling inference iterations rather than understanding that the paper is about training-time distribution evolution

additions.what: Changed desirable property to 'principled mechanism that governs how generated samples move or change position during training iterations'
additions.why: The student needs to think about sample movement during training, not consistency between inference steps

additions.what: Changed equilibrium property to specify 'generated samples stop moving when output distribution matches data distribution'
additions.why: The paper's equilibrium is about samples no longer drifting when distributions match - this needs to be clearer

additions.what: Changed interaction property to 'direct interactions between individual generated samples and individual real data samples to determine how samples should move'
additions.why: The paper uses pairwise interactions to compute a drift field - the student needs to think about sample-to-sample interactions

additions.what: Added property about 'mathematical properties that guarantee equilibrium is reached only when distributions match'
additions.why: The anti-symmetric property of the drifting field is crucial but the student hasn't considered mathematical constraints on the movement mechanism

additions.what: Added 'An underexplored direction is how the training process itself evolves distributions over time' to field_context
additions.why: To reinforce that this is about training-time evolution, not inference-time procedures

removals.what: Removed generic 'leveraging iterative nature of training' property
removals.why: Too vague - replaced with more specific properties about sample movement

removals.what: Removed generic 'using interactions between generated and real samples' property
removals.why: Too vague - replaced with more specific property about individual sample interactions determining movement

rationale.unchanged: Kept the basic problem framing about single-step generation and the contrast with iterative inference methods, as this correctly identifies the paper's goal
